items.title: Measuring spin-charge separation by an off-diagonal dissipative response
authors: Liang Tong, Shi Chen and Yu Chen
items.summary: Spin-charge separation in the 1D Hubbard model is a paradigmatic example of quantum fractionalization described by decoupled charge and spin sectors of a Tomonaga–Luttinger liquid. Despite the success in measuring velocity differences, it remains challenging to probe emergent excitations’ anomalous dimensions experimentally. We propose an off-diagonal dissipative response protocol, leveraging dissipative response theory, to directly detect spin-charge separation. By selectively dissipating spin- particles and measuring the spin- response, we uncover a universal temporal crossover: the response grows as at short times and crosses over to linear-in- growth at long times. Specifically, the intersection time between the short-time and long-time linear growth exhibits a linear dependence on , whose slope is proportional to with a prefactor that depends on the filling , with negligible residual dependence on over a broad parameter range. This prefactor cancels when comparing slopes at a fixed , allowing the relative variation of with interaction strength to be extracted directly without any absolute calibration. Concurrently, the coefficient of the short-time law encodes the sum of anomalous dimensions through its spatial power-law decay. This response signal vanishes in the noninteracting limit, where spin and charge are not separated. Our predictions, verified numerically via time-dependent density-matrix renormalization group with microscopic parameters linked to Luttinger parameters by Bethe-ansatz, establish off-diagonal dissipative response as a self-contained probe of quantum fractionalization in synthetic quantum matter.

items.title: Two phase transitions in modular multiplex networks
authors: Yael Kfir-Cohen, Dana Ben Porath, Bnaya Gross, Sergey Buldyrev and Shlomo Havlin
items.summary: Modular networks, such as critical infrastructures, are often built from distinct, densely connected modules (e.g. cities) that are sparsely interconnected. When such networks are gradually and randomly disrupted under a percolation process, they undergo two critical phase transitions. The first transition occurs when modules become isolated from one another, while the second corresponds to the collapse of the entire network, including the internal connectivity of the modules. Here, we study these phase transitions in modular multiplex networks and compare them with those observed in single-layer modular networks. We focus on models in which the modules are arranged and connected either as a short-range two-dimensional square lattice or as a long-range random regular (RR) network. We show here that these systems exhibit diverse transition behaviors, with some transitions occurring continuously and others abruptly; notably, one realistic model display two distinct abrupt transitions in the same system. By tuning the range of the inter-module connectivity between these two limits, we further show that the order of the spatial transition changes gradually from continuous to abrupt. For the modular RR multiplex, we further characterize the spatial transition through its scaling behavior, revealing signatures of a mixed-order phase transition. In addition, we analytically determine the critical threshold at which modules become disconnected. Our results highlight the crucial role of modular organization and the critical role of interdependence in shaping network vulnerabilities under failures.

items.title: Heterogeneous architectures enable a 138 × reduction in ph...
authors: Pranav S Mundada, Aleksei Khindanov, Yulun Wang, Claire L Edmunds, Paul Coote, Michael J Biercuk, Yuval Baum and Michael Hush
items.summary: Quantum computer hardware performance and scale have accelerated rapidly over the past few years, enabling real workloads to be run using hundreds of physical qubits, and industry roadmaps predict systems with hundreds of thousands of qubits coming online in the next decade. Moving to this scale requires major advances in quantum error correction (QEC) and its useful integration into real hardware systems. Despite significant theoretical and experimental QEC progress, quantum computer architecture has suffered a significant gap, with bottom-up physical-device-driven challenges largely disconnected from top-down QEC-code-driven considerations. In this work, we unify these two views, presenting a complete heterogeneous quantum computing architecture incorporating task-specific hardware selection and QEC encoding, and agnostic to code selection or physical qubit parameters. The architecture is based on the observation that due to the lengthy idling periods encountered in common algorithms, it can be advantageous to separate quantum processing operations from quantum memory, enabling expanded flexibility in qubit modality and code choice between subsystems. Our approach further enables special-purpose processing modules, and includes a full microarchitecture for fault-tolerant implementation of interfaces between quantum processing units and quantum memories. Using this architecture and a new fully featured compiler functioning across subsystems at the scale of logical qubits, we schedule and orchestrate a variety of algorithms down to hardware-specific instructions; a detailed accounting of all operations reveals up to reduction in algorithmic logical error and up to reduction in physical-qubit overhead compared to a monolithic baseline architecture. We then consider the factorization of 2048-bit RSA-integers; using an experimentally demonstrated grid-coupling topology, factoring RSA-2048 requires 381k physical qubits and 9.2 d, which can be reduced to 4.9 d via addition of an algorithm-specific accelerator for the Adder subroutine (requiring 439k qubits). Finally, assuming hypothetical long-range coupling, implementing quantum memory using qLDPC codes reduces the resources required for factoring to just 190k qubits and under 10 d. These results and the tooling we have built indicate that heterogeneous quantum-computer architectures can deliver significant, verifiable benefits on realistic hardware.

items.title: Theory of relativistic surface plasmon excitation on smooth surfaces by high-intensity lasers
authors: Bifeng Lei, Bin Qiao, Matt Zepf, Guoxing Xia and Carsten Welsch
items.summary: We present a classical theory of relativistic surface plasmon (RSP) excitation at smooth planar and cylindrical plasma-vacuum interfaces driven along the surface or channel axis by the ponderomotive force or carrier electric field of an intense laser pulse. Starting from Maxwell’s equations and a cold-fluid plasma response, we derive a general driven-mode equation and obtain analytical solutions for Gaussian sources. Excitation is governed by the overlap between the drive and the surface eigenfield, together with frequency and wavenumber matching. An infinite planar interface conserves in-plane momentum, while cylindrical geometry replaces one continuous tangential wavenumber with a discrete azimuthal index and retains axial phase-matching requirements. Within a frozen-quiver relativistic Drude model, the field shows saturation on planar surface, whereas cylindrical curvature mitigate this effect by modifies the mode dispersion and the field confinement. Preliminary particle-in-cell simulations show qualitative agreement with the predicted intensity dependence. Cylindrical symmetry also imposes source-dependent azimuthal selection rules, and the axisymmetric mode supports a nonzero on-axis accelerating field. These results clarify how surface geometry controls RSP excitation and provide a framework that can be extended to other geometries and driving mechanisms.

items.title: Nonlocal Josephson diode effect in series-connected triplet p -wave superconductors
authors: Juan Juan Wang and Jun Wang
items.summary: In this work, we investigate a series-connected Josephson junction (JJ) system composed of three triplet -wave superconductors. By tuning the -vector orientation angles of the triplet superconductors, we achieve efficient control over nonlocal spin and charge supercurrents. Utilizing the Andreev molecular states formed between the two adjacent JJs, we show a spin version of Josephson diode effect (sJDE) with an efficiency of over and arbitrary nonlocal control of supercurrents in the complete absence of macroscopic superconducting phase differences when a magnetic barrier is introduced. Moreover, the efficiency of the nonlocal JDE can be enhanced to over by optimizing the -vector configurations. Our results provide a new pathway for achieving nonlocal supercurrent control and high-efficiency JDE.

items.title: From Topological Order to Mixed-State Phases: A Ground-State Probe of Fractionalized Excitations
authors: Yunlong Zang, Yu-Bin Li and Shenghan Jiang
items.summary: How do we detect topological phases from a single ground state? Entanglement entropy and spectrum have long been the standard tools—but the reduced density matrix (RDM) itself contains far more information. We show that the RDM of a 2D topologically ordered system, expressed at the entanglement cut, realizes a 1D mixed-state phase. For the toric code phase, it is a 1D strong-to-weak spontaneous symmetry breaking (SW-SSB) phase, where deconfinement of anyons manifests as the short-range correlation of both charge and domain-wall in the RDM. The bulk e–m duality translates into a Kramers–Wannier self-duality of the SW-SSB phase. Extending the framework to gapped spin liquids, the global spin-rotation symmetry manifests as an additional weak symmetry for the 1D RDM. Spin-1/2 spinons result in a cusp on the disorder parameter of spin-rotation at θ = π, providing a direct, ground-state signature of symmetry fractionalization. We verify this prediction analytically using the matrix product density operator formalism and numerically for the kagome-lattice resonating valence bond state. The proposed observable requires only a single ground-state wavefunction, making it amenable to quantum simulation platforms.

items.title: Symmetry-Enforced Single-Pair Charge-Two Triple-Point Semimetals
authors: Hui-Jing Zheng, Ke-Xin Pang, Yun-Yun Bai, Yan Gao and Zhong-Yi Lu
items.summary: The Nielsen–Ninomiya theorem mandates that the net chiral charge of topological nodes in a crystal’s Brillouin zone must vanish, requiring them to appear in pairs. While realizing the absolute minimum of a single pair of topological nodes has been achieved for Weyl semimetals, hosting the minimal configuration of chiral charge-two (|C| = 2) triple-degenerate points (C-2 TPs) in a realistic electronic material remains an open challenge. By combining little-group constraints with both possible two-node orbit structures across all 1651 magnetic space groups (MSGs), we identify 21 MSGs without spin–orbit coupling (SOC) and 3 MSGs with SOC that are compatible with an isolated single pair of C-2 TPs. Guided by these symmetry criteria, we predict that the cubic boron allotrope P23-B36 acts as a premier electronic platform for this exotic phase. Owing to the negligible SOC of light boron atoms, the system behaves as a spinless semimetal, where the three crossing bands form exactly two symmetry-enforced C-2 TPs at the high-symmetry points Γ and R with chiralities C = +2 and C = 2, respectively. First-principles calculations reveal maximally extended double Fermi arcs on both the (001) and (110) surfaces, providing a distinct spectroscopic fingerprint for experimental detection. Our work establishes a rigorous symmetry-guided design framework for minimal multifold semimetals and identifies an elemental platform for exploring their intrinsic quantum transport phenomena.

items.title: Ultrasmall (3,0) Carbon Nanotube: a Superconducting Unit with Strong Electron–Phonon Coupling
authors: Zhenfeng Ouyang, Jing Jiang, Jian-Feng Zhang, Miao Gao, Kai Liu and Zhong-Yi Lu
items.summary: Based on density-functional first-principles calculations, we study the electronic structures, lattice dynamics, and electron–phonon coupling (EPC) properties of the ultrasmall one-dimensional (3,0) carbon nanotube (CNT). Our studies reveal that the (3,0) CNT hosts characteristic collective phonon modes, in which the corresponding atomic vibrations can significantly modulate the electronic self-consistent potential and induce strong EPC. Our results further show that the (3,0) CNT exhibits robust phonon-mediated superconductivity under ambient pressure, with a superconducting transition temperature reaching ~33 K (μ* = 0.10). We also find that although hole doping enhances the density of states (DOS) near the Fermi level, it simultaneously hardens the strongly coupled phonon modes and suppresses the total EPC. This result indicates that phonons play a more crucial role in the superconductivity of ultrasmall CNTs rather than the DOS alone. Therefore, we suggest that the ultrasmall (3,0) CNT can serve as a superconducting unit hosting phonon modes with strong EPC, and propose a strategy for discovering new phonon-mediated superconductors by identifying superconducting units.

items.title: Deep Learning Reveals a Correlation between Local Composition and Majorana Zero Modes in FeTe1-x Se x
authors: Qiheng Wang, Quanxin Hu, Yang Tian, Yong Huang, Bo Zhao, Baiqing Lv and Hong Ding
items.summary: Majorana zero modes (MZMs) in topological superconductors offer a promising route towards fault-tolerant quantum computation. Among candidate materials, the iron-based superconductor FeTe1-xSex has recently emerged as a robust and relatively clean platform for realizing and exploring MZMs. Yet MZMs in this material emerge only in a subset of magnetic vortices, and the origin of this spatially inhomogeneous yield remains unresolved. Here we develop a deep-learning framework for the in situ, high-throughput and standardized mapping of the top-layer Te/Se composition directly from scanning tunnelling microscopy topographs. By achieving atomically resolved compositional mapping with high fidelity, we quantify the local chemical disorder surrounding vortex cores. Combining these AI-derived atomic maps with MZM classifications obtained independently from vortex-core spectroscopy, we statistically analyze 61 vortices and find that MZMs are strongly enriched within a narrow window of local Te concentration, whereas vortices outside this window predominantly host Caroli–de Gennes–Matricon bound states without a zero-bias peak. These results identify local composition as a key statistical factor governing the uneven MZM yield in FeTe1-xSex, and establish an AI-assisted strategy for identifying and optimizing topological superconductors for device applications.

items.title: Quantum Gouy phase singularities in a propagating biphoton state
items.summary: Phase singularities are topological defects around which the phase winds by an integer multiple of . In entangled multiphoton states, they can emerge nonlocally in the joint wavefunction rather than in the field of either subsystem alone. Here we show that the quantum Gouy phase generates nonlocal phase singularities (NPSs) in the two-dimensional longitudinal propagation space of entangled photon pairs. We consider photon pairs produced via spontaneous parametric down-conversion pumped by a Laguerre–Gaussian beam, with the signal and idler photons propagating independently over different longitudinal distances. The accumulated radial-mode-dependent Gouy phases induce destructive interference among biphoton spatial-mode components, producing isolated intensity nulls with quantized phase winding. For a pump with radial mode number , the NPS topological charges have magnitude , whereas their propagation positions and charge signs are governed by the Rayleigh ranges of the pump and phase-matching functions. We further identify the radial-mode structure required for their formation, showing that separable biphoton states cannot support isolated longitudinal NPSs. Our results extend nonlocal singular optics from transverse spatial correlations to longitudinal propagation dynamics and establish propagation distance as a coordinate space for topological structures in entangled photon pairs.

items.title: Model predictive quantum control: a modular approach for efficient and robust quantum optimal control
items.summary: Model predictive control (MPC) is one of the most successful modern control methods. It relies on repeatedly solving a finite-horizon optimal control problem and applying the beginning piece of the optimal input. In this paper, we develop a modular framework for improving efficiency and robustness of quantum optimal control (QOC) via MPC. We first provide a tutorial introduction to basic concepts of MPC from a QOC perspective. We then present multiple MPC schemes, ranging from simple approaches to more sophisticated schemes which admit stability guarantees. This yields a modular framework which can be used 1) to improve efficiency of open-loop QOC and 2) to improve robustness of closed-loop quantum control by incorporating feedback. We demonstrate these benefits with numerical results, where we benchmark the proposed methods against competing approaches.

items.title: Noise-induced thermalization in quantum systems
authors: Sameer Dambal, Yu Zhang, Eric R Bittner and Pavan Hosur
items.summary: In the current noisy intermediate-scale quantum era, noise is widely regarded as the primary obstacle to achieving fault-tolerant quantum computation. However, certain stages of the quantum computing pipeline can, in fact, benefit from this noise. In this work, we exploit the eigenstate thermalization hypothesis to show that an number of noise occurrences can accelerate a fundamental task in quantum computing—the preparation of Gibbs states. We demonstrate this behavior using classical simulations with Haar-random and phase-flip noise, respectively, on a spin-1/2 chain with a local Hamiltonian. Our non-integrable model sees faster thermalization in the presence of noise, while our integrable model reaches a state that lies between a generalized Gibbs state and a Gibbs state due to noise. Since certifying a local Gibbs state is relatively easy on a quantum computer, our approach provides a new practical solution to a key problem in quantum computing. More broadly, these results establish a new paradigm in which noise can be harnessed on quantum computers, enabling practical advantages before the years of fault-tolerance.

items.title: Interaction Between Yin-Yang Vortex States and Topological Edge States in UTe2
authors: Yuguang Wang, 宇光 王, Yuanji Li, 元骥 李, Dengpeng Yuan, 登鹏 袁, Ruotong Yin, 若彤 尹, Jiashuo Gong, 佳硕 巩, Jiakang Zhang, 嘉康 张, Shiyuan Wang, 适源 王, Weiyi Liu, 唯一 刘, Shiyong Tan, 世勇 谭, Dong-Lai Feng, 东来 封, Ya-Jun Yan and 亚军 闫
items.summary: UTe2, a strong candidate for spin-triplet superconductivity, hosts novel step-edge states and Yin-Yang vortices on its (011) surface, both of which are intimately connected to topological surface states. However, the interaction between these two types of states remains unexplored. Here, we use scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy (STM/STS) to investigate the coupling between step-edge states and Yin-Yang vortex states in UTe2. We uncover pronounced edge–vortex interactions, and find that the resulting in-gap spectral reconstruction is spatially asymmetric and depends sensitively on the position of the step edge relative to the vortex. Most strikingly, when the Yang vortex directly coincides with the step edge, the zero-energy conductance peak, a candidate Majorana mode signal, is locally suppressed. Our findings reveal an unexplored interplay between topological boundary states and vortex bound states in a spin-triplet superconductor and establish step edges as a local tuning factor for vortex zero modes, providing possibilities for spatially selective manipulation of candidate Majorana modes through engineered boundary geometries.

This effect explains why observed CISS signals are much larger than predicted by simple orbital models.

Issue Editorial Masthead
The Roaming Bethe Roots: An Effective Bethe Ansatz Beyond Integrability
authors: Wenlong Zhao, 文龙 赵, Yunfeng Jiang, 云峰 江, Rui-Dong Zhu and 睿东 朱
items.summary: We propose an effective Bethe ansatz (EBA) for solving quantum many-body systems near an integrable point. Our approach retains the functional form of the Bethe wave function while renormalizing the Bethe roots to account for integrability-breaking interactions. These effective roots are determined by minimizing physically motivated cost functions. The resulting off-shell Bethe states serve as approximate eigenstates of the non-integrable models. We assess the quality of the approximation using various physical observables, including the energy eigenvalue, state fidelity, and bipartite entanglement entropy. Our tests show that for models with weak integrability-breaking, the EBA provides a high-quality approximation to the exact eigenstates over a wide range of deformation parameters. In contrast, for models with strong integrability-breaking interactions, the efficacy of EBA degrades relatively quickly as the deformation parameter increases. The efficacy of the method thus offers a useful probe for characterizing the strength of integrability breaking. Within its regime of accuracy, it also provides a new representation of the eigenstates of nearly integrable models, enabling one to exploit the algebraic structure inherited from integrability.

items.title: Unveiling the Elusive Σ(1380) Resonance through Coupled-Channel Dynamics in Λ c + ηπ + Λ Reaction
authors: Wen-Tao Lyu, 文韬 吕, Si-Wei Liu, 思威 刘, Jia-Jun Wu, 佳俊 吴, De-Min Li, 德民 李, En Wang and 恩 王
items.summary: We investigate the Λc+ ηπ +Λ decay measured by the Belle and BESIII Collaborations, focusing on the possible role of the Σ(1380) state with spin-parity J P=1/2−. In our theoretical framework, the Λ(1670) and a0(980) are dynamically generated from meson–baryon and meson–meson final-state interactions, respectively, and the corresponding line shapes of these two states used here are applicable to all relevant hadronic reactions. Furthermore, the contributions from the intermediate Σ(1385) resonance and the possible Σ(1380) state are included explicitly. By comparing the invariant mass and angular distributions obtained with and without the Σ(1380) state, we demonstrate that this state plays an important role in improving the description of the experimental data. We also identify the kinematic regions most sensitive to the possible Σ(1380) contribution. Future high-precision measurements of this process will be instrumental for testing the existence of the Σ state with J P=1/2−.

items.summary: Training artificial intelligence (AI) for experimental science usually requires huge collections of labeled data, which many techniques, such as angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), simply do not have. Na et al. show that synthetic ARPES data can fill the gap. They develop a high-fidelity ARPES simulator, aurelia, and train an AI model capable of judging the quality of real measurement data and of picking up the best spot to measure on the sample surface more precisely than a conventional analysis, highlighting the potential of AI-assisted experiments.
